chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umeyr, and someone else, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Is the prayer in the house of Fatima (peace be upon her) like the prayer in the garden?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'And superior (to it).'

key_terms.الرَّوْضَةِ: The garden (specifically the Rawdah in Mecca or Medina)

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of praying in the house of Fatima (peace be upon her) compared to the Rawdah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Jameel ibn Darraj inquires whether the reward for prayer in the house of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) equals that of the Rawdah (the garden of the Prophet in Medina). Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) not only confirms the equality but elevates it by stating it is superior (*afdal*), highlighting the unique spiritual status of her dwelling as an extension of the Prophet’s sanctity. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt’s physical spaces as vessels of divine grace, linking the domestic sphere of the Prophet’s family to the sacred geography of Medina.
